response.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT p.SEX AS sex, AVG(l.CPK * 1.0 / l.GPT) AS a FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE l.CPK IS NOT NULL AND l.GPT IS NOT NULL AND l.GPT <> 0 GROUP BY p.SEX), m1 AS (SELECT AVG(a) AS m FROM r), k AS (SELECT r.a AS a FROM r, m1 WHERE r.a > m1.m), m2 AS (SELECT AVG(a) AS m FROM k), f AS (SELECT k.a AS a FROM k, m2 WHERE k.a > m2.m) SELECT AVG(a) AS avg_ratio, AVG(a - (SELECT m FROM m1)) AS avg_excess_over_first_mean, AVG(a - (SELECT m FROM m2)) AS avg_excess_over_second_mean FROM f;

assumptions.assumption: A ratio is missing when CPK or GPT is NULL, or when GPT is 0 because the division is undefined. Those tests are excluded.
Patients with NULL SEX form one group, and patients with '' SEX form a separate group. Both are included in the means.
The ratio is computed in floating point (CPK*1.0/GPT) to avoid integer division. Group averages are plain means of per-test ratios. 'Above' means strictly greater than.
